anchors.note: Root cause. In the printer's parent walk, the intermediate optional node is neither `CIL_BLOCK` nor `bi_node`, so the `else` arm assumes `curr->data` is a `struct cil_blockinherit`. On a `struct cil_optional`, reading `((struct cil_blockinherit *)curr->data)->block` fetches bytes at offset 8 of the optional object, which is really `optional->datum.name` and therefore the pointer to the 2-byte string `"o"`.

Sink. `NODE(...)` treats the fake `block` value from step 8 as a `struct cil_symtab_datum *` and dereferences its `nodes` field. Because that value is actually the 2-byte heap string `"o"` allocated from step 1, the dereference performs the saved 8-byte read exactly at the start of that 2-byte allocation, producing the ASan heap-buffer-overflow report.

Inside the recursive-blockinherit printer, every non-`CIL_BLOCK` ancestor is treated as though `curr->data` were a `struct cil_blockinherit`. When the ancestor is actually `CIL_OPTIONAL`, this cast reinterprets `optional->datum.name` as the `block` field of a blockinherit object.

ASan crash site. `NODE(...)` dereferences the misread pointer value as a `struct cil_symtab_datum *`; on this path that pointer is actually the 2-byte pooled string `"o"`, so the dereference performs the reported 8-byte heap out-of-bounds read.
